_declared_fixture: DECLARED FIXTURE, not a real external rule. No real external rule exists anywhere in this system, and no code path fetches one: there is no discovery and no search, by decision. These four entries were written by hand to exercise the two-rule-set separation, and they are the ONLY external rules in existence. Anything that reads this file is reading a fixture and must say so.

_why_each_entry.EXT-001: OVERLAPS AND DISAGREES with a convention on severity. Must be detected, refused, and put to the operator. This is the row the conflict record never had.
_why_each_entry.EXT-002: OVERLAPS AND AGREES. Must NOT be reported as a conflict: both apply. An agreeing rule reported as a conflict would make the operator arbitrate a question nobody is asking.
_why_each_entry.EXT-003: DOES NOT OVERLAP at all. Must NOT be reported as a conflict: both apply, on different subjects.
_why_each_entry.EXT-004: OVERLAPS and declares a conditional suspension the convention does not. That is a disagreement about when the rule applies, not about how severe it is, and it is detected as one.

external_rules.rule: A reading outside the adjacent range is reported for information only.
A missing calibration date is an irregularity.
An operator initial is recorded beside each entry.
A reading outside the adjacent range is an irregularity, unless the entry carries a fault acknowledgement.
